sense: speak to; call by a name or title

terms.gloss: address, speak to; call (someone by a name or title)
evidence: Cic. Q. fr. 2.8.1: ut mē et appellēs et interpellēs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to accost, address, to speak to, call upon (very freq. and class.)”; with two accusatives, to address someone as something. Not appellō, appellere, drive towards.

terms.gloss: speak to, address (a person or a crowd)
evidence: Traupman 176, 268: senātum adloquentur, will address the senate
terms.comment: Also spelled adloquor. Lewis & Short: rare before Augustus (twice in Cicero), common after; used of a general addressing his troops. A speech to a gathering is ōrātiō (see speech).

phrases.english: when he had addressed Fabius as “father”

phrases.latin: tū vērō ut mē et appellēs et interpellēs et obloquāre et colloquāre velim. quid enim mihi suāvius?
phrases.english: I do want you to speak to me, interrupt me, contradict me, talk with me. What could be sweeter to me?
What are you waiting for? Speak to him!
